items.title: Slay the Spire 2 lead says the 'garbage' placeholder art is important and gen AI would ruin it
items.excerpt: Slay the Spire 2's lead defends deliberately rough hand-made placeholder art in Early Access, arguing generative AI 'would ruin it' because polished AI fill-ins make players judge an unfinished build as a finished 1.0 — a craft-and-iteration case against gen AI in the art pipeline.

items.title: Mario Kart Wii is being rebuilt for PC, but the project's AI vibe-coding instantly soured many Nintendo fans
items.excerpt: A fan effort billed as 'the first static recompilation of a Wii game' has drawn backlash after the team leaned on AI vibe-coding, reopening the debate over whether AI-assisted tooling yields quality PC ports or low-effort output that erodes trust in preservation projects.

items.title: "Steam's required AI disclosure is the right move": Devs say gen AI should be called out in games and support Valve's store mandate
items.excerpt: Developers push back on Epic's Tim Sweeney over Valve's AI labels, arguing that disclosing generative-AI content shipped to players is a baseline transparency and creative-credit standard — a workflow/ethics question every storefront and studio now has to answer.

items.title: Steam Week in Review: more than half of new Steam games will have an AI-disclosure by 2027-2028
items.excerpt: A census of Steam releases finds 30.8% of 2026 games now carry an AI-content disclosure, up from 10.9% in 2024, with the trajectory pointing at a majority of new releases labelling generative-AI content within two years — a fast-shifting norm for how studios ship AI-made assets.

items.title: iOS developer made a Capybara game using vibe-coding and won $25,000
items.excerpt: An iOS developer built a Capybara food-delivery game almost entirely by 'vibe-coding' with Claude Code and won a $25,000 prize — a concrete example of AI coding agents collapsing the barrier for a solo creator to ship a finished mobile game.
